BLOCKER: affected_files lists only `store-registry.json`, yet the contract ships `migrations/0025_event_subscriptions_dispatch.up.sql`, its down file, and `go/edpdata/event_dispatcher.go`; the declared change surface does not match the approved artifacts (traceability/rollback cannot be verified against declared files).
CL-015: `ac_evidence`/`coverage` entries for AC-1 and AC-2 carry no candidate SHA; evidence is unpinned, so Gate-2 verification of the exactly-once-effective and single-writer ACs is unprovable.

Single-writer invariant (AC-2/FR-2) has no stated enforcement mechanism (lease/advisory lock/ownership gate) for `event_subscriptions` upserts; "one writer" is asserted, not designed or tested, so the P0 AC cannot be met as specified.
MAJOR: AC-1 "exactly-once-effective" depends on idempotent transport behavior, but transports (E5) are out of scope; the design must state how the AC is satisfied with a fake/adapter contract, otherwise the AC is untestable end-to-end.
Dispatcher cursor/checkpoint persistence is unspecified; where the read cursor lives risks becoming a de-facto second event store, conflicting with the "no second event store" data rule.

Rollback is inconsistent: gate says "Revert the change", spec says "drop new tables" / run 0025 down — destructive rollback drops `event_deliveries`/`event_delivery_dlq`, losing retained delivery and DLQ data with no stated backup verification step (guardrail 1).
No ordering/idempotency invariant statement for cursor advancement vs delivery-row commit (at-least-once window), and no migration-interrupted recovery path (guardrails 5, 6).
`affected_components`, `risks` are "Not specified"; failure/blast-radius (scheduler/worker/DB down, DLQ growth, alert ownership per CL-014) is not addressed.
MINOR: Observability is only "EventMetrics signals + delivery status": no concrete metric names/labels (subscription_id, outcome, retry age, DLQ depth) or runbook pointer for diagnosing stuck dispatch.
Authz boundary for the operator upsert path (FR-2) is not defined beyond "tenant-scoped store"; no explicit statement that runtime DB roles are subject to RLS (no BYPASSRLS).
`data_lifecycle` says "DLQ retained" with no retention/redaction policy or cleanup owner.
Test matrix lists only `go test ./...`; no explicit concurrency test or backoff/DLQ-bound test named in coverage despite being in `approach`.
NIT: `config_contract: 'N/A': 'no new env'` — but bounded batch size and retry/backoff schedule need a documented default; "no new env" should say where those are fixed.
Traceability maps both FR-1 and FR-2 to the same single test file; separate evidence per AC would tighten Gate-2 verification.
SUMMARY: Design is directionally right (reuse edpdata, additive migration, no second store) but not review-ready: declared files omit the migration and dispatcher, AC evidence lacks candidate SHA, and the single-writer invariant has no enforcement mechanism.
Top risks: unpinned/unverifiable AC evidence, destructive rollback losing DLQ/delivery data, and exactly-once-effective claimed while transports are out of scope.
Require correction of file/SHA traceability and an explicit writer-arbitration + cursor-storage design before Gate 1.5.
